papers.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
papers.abstract: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

papers.title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
papers.abstract: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

papers.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

papers.title: High-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial
papers.abstract: We prove that, above a constant temperature threshold, Gibbs states of local noncommuting qudit Hamiltonians exhibit exponential decay of mutual information and conditional mutual information (CMI). Specifically, we prove exponential decay of the CMI for arbitrary spatial tripartitions $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ which need not comprise the entire system, thereby establishing a \textit{uniform Markov property} for high-temperature Gibbs states. A central obstruction to proving such bounds is that conventional cluster expansions for the logarithm of reduced Gibbs states can fail to converge due to noncommutativity. Our main insight is to construct a classical representation of the Gibbs state using an overcomplete basis. Although such representations generally involve negative quasiprobability weights, we show that a decomposition based on projective 2-designs admits a convergent cluster expansion with strictly positive weights at sufficiently high temperatures, allowing us to circumvent the obstruction. The separability of high-temperature Gibbs states is a natural byproduct of this decomposition. Finally, in the context of mixed-state phases of matter, our results imply that high-temperature Gibbs states belong to the same mixed-state phase as the maximally mixed state.

papers.title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
papers.abstract: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM). Both the GFM and IFM predict the metric motion between consecutive frames, and a lightweight learned fusion head quantifies the reliability of each estimate and blends them in a single forward pass. Across nine datasets recorded from cars, legged and ground robots, and handheld and head- mounted devices, AnyVIO reduces the metric position error of its visual model by 36% while publishing each pose esti- mate 70 ms after an image is received. We further deploy AnyVIO onboard two real vehicles at up to 140 km/h, where it remains accurate in poor lighting and heavy dust.

papers.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
papers.abstract: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

papers.title: Path-Independent Deleveraging Rules
papers.abstract: We characterise path-independent auto-deleveraging (ADL) rules as an extended log-exponential family. Immunity to account splitting, merging and reopening further restrict the class. Homogeneity (essentially) restricts the class to a one-parameter family ordered by both fairness and platform risk. Its split-proof members continuously interpolate between proportional division and water-filling. Among these rules, decreasing the parameter reduces risk at the cost of increasing inequality in how accounts are treated. This suggests selecting the parameter through an ex-ante calibration to a risk bound on historical data to choose a maximally fair rule subject to that bound. A counterfactual replay of Hyperliquid's ADL episode on 10 October 2025 finds that a range of intermediate parameters significantly improves on the observed allocation in both burden dispersion and subsequent risk statistics.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
papers.abstract: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(\pi/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(\pi/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.

papers.title: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
papers.abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.

papers.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
papers.abstract: Quantum tunneling transverse to the inflaton trajectory can produce $10^6$--$10^8M_\odot$ primordial black holes at the abundance of JWST's little red dots, without the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by limits on CMB spectral distortions. Rare vacuum bubbles nucleate during a brief interval of inflation and later form black holes, with adjustable mass and abundance and a narrow mass spectrum of percent-level width. The leading constraint, from accretion, is satisfied for a population matching the bright little red dots even if all the emitted radiation escapes as hard X-rays.

papers.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
papers.abstract: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.

papers.title: Every galaxy is a radio source: a stellar-mass dependent minimum 150 MHz luminosity identified in the LoTSS Deep Fields
papers.abstract: The second data release of the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) Deep Fields includes the deepest wide-field 150 MHz mosaics in existence, covering the ELAIS-N1 field. Combining these radio observations with star-formation rate (SFR) and stellar mass estimates for 113,228 near-infrared selected galaxies derived using Prospector, we re-examine the relationship between galaxies' 150 MHz luminosities ($L_{150\rm{MHz}}$), SFRs and stellar masses. We not only recover the established radio luminosity-SFR relation and its dependence on stellar mass, but also discover a mass-dependent minimum radio luminosity that is independent of SFR. This behaviour is especially evident in galaxies with low specific SFR (sSFR $\equiv$ SFR/$M_*$), at $L_{150\rm MHz} \sim 10^{20}-10^{22}$ W Hz$^{-1}$, where star-forming galaxies are expected to dominate. The non-stellar emission is consistent with low-level accretion onto supermassive black holes (i.e. weak active galactic nuclei, AGN), spanning effective Eddington-scaled accretion rates $\lambda_{\rm Edd} \sim 10^{-5}-10^{-4}$, suggesting that radio emission due to accretion is widespread and effectively continuous. A two-component model combining star formation- and accretion-driven emission reproduces the observed trends, demonstrating that AGN activity can bias radio-based SFR estimates. The low radio luminosities probed in this work provide a first glimpse of the populations that will be routinely accessible with future facilities such as LOFAR 2.0 and the Square Kilometre Array.

papers.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
papers.abstract: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.

papers.title: Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
papers.abstract: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.

papers.title: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation through Shared Prediction and Refinement
papers.abstract: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement. To address task interference during distillation, we separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation and introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD). This procedure transfers prediction and refinement behaviors from specialized teachers into a shared student through local velocity matching under their respective sampling and history policies. {Extensive experiments demonstrate that ScaleWorld achieves high-quality world generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.

papers.title: Additive Fr\'echet Regression for Random Objects
papers.abstract: Regression analysis for complex data taking values in a general metric space has gained increasing attention in recent years, particularly in the context of Fr\'echet regression with Euclidean predictors $\mathbb{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{p}$. However, local Fr\'echet regression, while more flexible than global Fr\'echet regression, suffers from the curse of dimensionality for the case of multivariate predictors. To address this issue while maintaining model flexibility, we introduce a framework of additive structured nonparametric regression when responses are situated in a general metric space. Overcoming the challenge of the lack of vector space structure in general metric spaces where the responses reside requires a novel approach that incorporates the additive structure via projection operators. This leads to a unified framework of additive regression for a wide range of response types, including one-dimensional distributions in Wasserstein space, network data represented by graph Laplacians and spherical data equipped with geodesic distances, among others. We establish pointwise and uniform consistency, including convergence rates, for the proposed additive Fr\'echet regression estimators, using smooth backfitting. The practical utility of this additive model is demonstrated through applications to brain connectivity network analysis using resting-state fMRI data and distributional physical activity data.

papers.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
papers.abstract: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

papers.title: BRUCE (Bayesian Rio Urban Climate Estimator): spatiotemporal interpolation of air temperature from heterogeneous sensor networks for operational heat monitoring
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization of intra-urban temperature variability is essential for heat-health surveillance, yet official monitoring networks are too sparse to resolve fine-scale gradients, particularly in Global South cities. We present BRUCE, a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model, fitted with the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) and a Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) spatial component, that fuses four heterogeneous temperature sources for Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: official weather stations, low-cost IoT sensors, citizen-science personal weather stations and ERA5-Land reanalysis. The model accounts for class- and station-specific measurement bias and estimates a continuous spatial field that evolves day to day through an autoregressive (AR1) structure. Fitted independently to nine monthly windows (January, June, November; 2023--2025), the elevation coefficient was significant in all windows and of consistent magnitude in eight ($-$1.08 to $-$1.38 \textdegree{}C per SD). In leave-region-out cross-validation against LCZ4r, accuracy was comparable (RMSE differences within station-level bootstrap uncertainty in all three windows), while BRUCE produced predictions at every held-out station, including those where LCZ4r is masked, and preserved finer-scale spatial structure than LCZ4r's discrete zone classification. Applied to 241 primary care territories, BRUCE's posterior exceedance probabilities allowed 96 to be classified with high confidence (model-based classifications), whereas a constant-width interval derived from LCZ4r cross-validation errors supported confident classification of none. The framework offers a statistically principled, operationally viable basis for intra-urban heat monitoring in data-heterogeneous settings.

papers.title: Bridging the Discovery Gap in Solid Dataspaces with a Semantic Data Catalog
papers.abstract: Dataspaces are an emerging concept to enable secure and controlled data sharing between multiple stakeholders. However, most existing dataspace architectures, such as those based on the concepts of IDSA (International Data Spaces Association) and Gaia-X, are heavily concept-driven and require significant effort to implement, making it difficult to quickly build a functional dataspace. Solid (Social Linked Data) offers a compelling alternative by providing a lighter and more practical approach. However, for Solid to function as a true dataspace, like traditional dataspaces, it must be built in a decentralized manner, i.e., the dataspace must consist of more than a single Solid server. However, this decentralization introduces a key challenge: Data Discovery. Unlike traditional dataspace architectures, which often include predefined components such as data catalogs to facilitate data discovery and access, Solid does not inherently provide such mechanisms. As a result, managing and locating relevant data across multiple Solid servers and pods becomes a significant barrier to usability. To address this gap, we present a FAIR-compliant data catalog for Solid. Our catalog follows the FAIR principles (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability) by integrating semantic models that describe all available data sources within the Solid ecosystem. This approach enables enhanced data discovery, improves accessibility through standardized metadata, enhances interoperability between different data sources, and promotes data reuse across applications. By bridging this critical gap, our catalog improves the usability of Solid-based dataspaces, making them a viable option for decentralized and open data ecosystems, such as smart city applications.

papers.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
papers.abstract: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $\theta=\pi$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

papers.title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
papers.abstract: Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search. Indyk and Xu introduced the notion of $\alpha$-reachable graphs, which include graphs built by DiskANN's slow-preprocessing construction, and proved that greedy search achieves an approximation factor of $\tfrac{\alpha+1}{\alpha-1}$. Independently, Al-Jazzazi et al. proposed adaptive beam search (ABS) with a relaxation parameter $\gamma > 0$, showing a $\tfrac{2}{\gamma}$ approximation on navigable graphs ($\alpha \approx 1$), where greedy search admits no guarantees. In this work, we unify and generalize these results by proving that ABS with parameter $\gamma$ on $\alpha$-reachable graphs achieves an approximation of $\tfrac{\alpha+1}{\alpha(\gamma+1)-1}$ for any metric. Moreover, on sorted $\alpha$-reachable graphs (introduced by Gollapudi et al.) under the $\ell_2$ metric, we obtain the tighter bound $\max\bigl(\tfrac{\alpha}{\alpha(\gamma+1)-1}, \tfrac{\alpha^{2}+1}{\alpha^{2}(\gamma+1)-1}\bigr)$. Beyond these theoretical results, we design a beam predictor using features inspired by fine-grained analysis of ABS, trained via a constrained objective that minimizes mean distance computations subject to a target recall. On three 100-million-point benchmarks, using graphs built by DiskANN's practical construction, beam predictor lowers mean query latency on SSD-resident indices at matched recall by up to $29.6\%$ relative to classical beam search (CBS). Relative to ABS, it is faster in $11$ of $15$ settings, by up to $6.5\%$, and at most $1.4\%$ slower in the other $4$; at $95\%$ recall, its advantage over ABS grows from $0.8$--$4.2\%$ for $100$ neighbors to $4.6$--$5.6\%$ for $500$ neighbors. In memory, it needs $1.3$--$23.7\%$ fewer distance computations than CBS and $0.0$--$3.9\%$ fewer than ABS.

papers.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
papers.abstract: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field. We illustrate the capabilities of this technique by applying it to two canonical problems. First, we directly observe the self-similar evolution of the velocity field in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows. Second, we map out the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, explicitly demonstrating the quantization of velocity circulation.

papers.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
papers.abstract: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective. We analyze generation realism through distributional metrics and embedding-space visualizations, evaluate downstream utility through leave-one-subject-out HAR classification, and present a PatchDecoder for approximate raw waveform reconstruction. Our diffusion decoder achieves a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) macro-F1 of 0.68, demonstrating that generated tokens are realistic enough to train a classifier that transfers to real data. Combining synthetic-token augmentation with a 320-dimensional gravity-aware feature representation raises LOSO macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809 over a real-only baseline across 51 subjects on the WISDM benchmark, with statistically significant gains concentrated in the most challenging activity classes. These results demonstrate that high-fidelity generation in a pretrained encoder's representation space is achievable and practically useful for cross-subject HAR augmentation.

papers.title: Query-Optimal Quantum Minimum Finding from Numerical Estimators
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum minimum-finding algorithm for objectives accessed via numerical estimators that avoids the logarithmic query overhead of amplifying the confidence of estimates before the search. A coherent estimator that is $\varepsilon$-accurate with probability at least $2/3$ on each of $N$ labels suffices to find a $2\varepsilon$-optimal label using $O(\sqrt N)$ base-estimator queries at constant confidence. The query bound and the additive-error constant are separately worst-case optimal. More generally, suppose a preparation assigns probability mass at least a known $p$ to objective values at most $a$. Without knowing $a$ or the prepared distribution, our algorithm returns a candidate and an estimate $v$ such that, jointly with constant probability, $v$ is $\varepsilon$-accurate for the candidate and $v\le a+\varepsilon$. The algorithm uses $O(p^{-1/2})$ queries to each of the preparation and estimator oracles in the worst case, and the selected candidate can be retained as a quantum state. For preparation width $s_P$ and estimator workspace width $w$, it requires $O(s_P+w+\log\log(4/p))$ qubits, independently of the requested confidence. Applications give worst-case optimal $\Theta(\sqrt N/\eta)$ queries for selecting an $\eta$-optimal bounded expectation, and guided ground-energy estimation using $O(\omega^{-1})$ preparations and $O((\omega\eta)^{-1})$ elementary controlled-evolution queries at constant confidence, where $\omega$ is a lower bound on the guiding state's ground-space amplitude overlap.

papers.title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
papers.abstract: Arithmetic operations are a fundamental building block in the design of quantum algorithms, with their implementation cost expected to have a significant impact on the viability of a wide variety of quantum applications. In this work, we present novel algorithms for a number of in-place quantum arithmetic operations that are highly efficient in terms of their space and gate count overheads compared to the current state-of-the-art. We show that in-place modular multiplication of integers, modulo a power of two, can be performed with either a classical or quantum odd multiplier using $O(n^{1+\epsilon})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $\epsilon >0$. We then show that standard in-place integer multiplication can be performed with a non-zero classical or quantum multiplier using $O(n^{1+\epsilon})$ gates for any $\epsilon>0$, with no ancilla qubits required for the classical multiplier and a logarithmic number of ancilla qubits for the quantum. Using our quantum modular multiplication algorithm, we also show that in-place modular inversion, modulo a power of two, can be performed using $O(n^{1+\epsilon})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $\epsilon>0$. To our knowledge, these are the first quantum algorithms achieving both subquadratic gate counts and sublinear ancilla counts for each of the considered in-place operations. All but one of these fast operations are optimal in terms of memory, only requiring enough space to store the output of the operation, which overwrites the input directly. We present our multiplication algorithms as consequences of a single unified theorem, which may find further application within quantum arithmetic.

papers.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.

papers.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
papers.abstract: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/

papers.title: An Efficient Algorithm for Matroid Cups
papers.abstract: We design a polynomial-time algorithm for matroid cups with $O(1)$ discrepancy. Our matroid cups algorithm design consists of a sequence of reductions to simpler instances, culminating in $O(n)$ instances of matroid cups where the matroid has rank 1.

papers.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
papers.abstract: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

papers.title: Local orbital magnetization and Chern markers from equilibrium local currents
papers.abstract: Local currents carry the orbital magnetization of a macroscopic sample and are key for modeling inhomogeneous magnetic materials and for understanding magnetoelectric and topological responses. However, producing realistic simulated images of local currents in inhomogeneous systems remains challenging. Building upon recent work on stochastic estimation methods for tight-binding models, we show that all matrix elements of positive semidefinite operators defined on a lattice can be obtained at once from a single set of filtered random vectors. This eliminates the need for independent simulations previously required for off-diagonal elements, which significantly speeds up the calculation of spatial maps of local currents. Further, we express bond currents in terms of loop currents that obey a discrete Poisson equation, with the current vorticity acting as the source term. Its solution yields a local orbital magnetization. In analogy with the global St\v{r}eda relation, the derivative of this magnetization with respect to the chemical potential defines a new local Chern marker. Built entirely from bond currents, it requires no position operator and is not bound by the zero-sum rule of projector markers in open samples. Hence, it is free of boundary-compensation artifacts, and its sample average converges to the bulk Chern number in a controlled fashion.

papers.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
papers.abstract: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation. Across multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, OracleImitator matches or outperforms existing AFA methods across the budget range, recovering 90% of the attainable accuracy gain at under a quarter of the acquisition cost. Because the teacher is an explicit algorithmic object rather than an implicit optimization target, we can also measure directly how much of its ranking is recoverable by a policy restricted to what is visible at deployment.

papers.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
papers.abstract: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $\Gamma(2)$ and $\Gamma_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $\Gamma(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

papers.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

papers.title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
papers.abstract: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. However, how to construct proxies and prompts for optimal downstream quality remains underexplored, as do the capabilities and limitations of this paradigm. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. The results reveal task-dependent trade-offs: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while medium-grained proxies favor consistency. Physics simulation and proxy-aligned prompting further improve average quality. Guided by these findings, we introduce Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting. Its multi-agent harness preserves scene assets and guides repairs through visual inspection and independent review. Experiments demonstrate leading instruction following on VTR and scene consistency on R2M, improved physical plausibility over direct generation, and higher visual realism than the compared Code2Video baselines. Long-video evaluations further show gains in event structure and consistency across successive interactions, while revealing limitations in transition stability and adherence to scene settings.

papers.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
papers.abstract: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions. A detectable signal can remain possible for a sufficiently small tensor-to-scalar ratio, but only at the cost of an extremely large enhancement of the TSS vertex. Thus, while a future search for large scale parity violation is worth pursuing, generating a detectable signal within a consistent effective theory is highly nontrivial.

papers.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
papers.abstract: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples. We detect tangential alignment of blue disc galaxies at $22.5\sigma$ and radial alignment of red spheroidal galaxies at $65\sigma$. By measuring the alignment signal separately around overdensities and underdensities, we show that each of these alignments has the scale and environmental dependence of a linear response to the cosmic tidal field; a response purely quadratic in the Gaussian tidal field, as in classic tidal torque theory is ruled out.

papers.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
papers.abstract: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality. Prior constructions assume sampled rollouts are conditionally independent. We show this assumption fails in practice: reasoning streams are positively correlated through shared reasoning prefixes or across-prompt heterogeneity, changing not merely certificate efficiency but the hypothesis certified. Modeling dependence via a per-unit latent state (the random-effects / intraclass-correlation structure) induces exchangeable, equi-correlated increments with correlation $\rho$. Correlation splits the single null into a realized null about the drawn belief and a population null about average model behavior, which coincide only when $\rho=0$. We show: (i) the standard betting e-process remains anytime-valid for the realized null, not the population null; (ii) read as a population-null test, a suitable mixture has asymptotic crossing probability at least $\pi=P(\mu(Z)>0)$, potentially exceeding nominal $\epsilon$; (iii) the within-unit mean's effective sample size saturates at $1/\rho$, so extra within-unit rollouts cannot restore population validity; and (iv) a prompt-level e-process restores population validity, with optimal allocation at one rollout per prompt under a pure rollout budget. Simulations and Claude Haiku 4.5 rollouts confirm this regime dependence: on GSM8K ($\hat{\rho}=0.435$, $\hat{\theta}=+0.96$) the gap is dormant, whereas on AIME ($\hat{\rho}=0.480$, $\hat{\theta}=-0.15$) the single-unit rule crosses on 24% of prompts at nominal $\epsilon=0.05$, while the prompt-level procedure declines (0.00). This correctness result identifies which reliability claim an anytime-valid certificate actually supports under dependence.

papers.title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
papers.abstract: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $\kappa$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $\omega=m\Omega_{\rm H}-ij\kappa$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $\Omega_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $\kappa$. These local statements leave the QNM spectrum unchanged but matter for merger ringdowns, because a source falling through the horizon drives the exterior at the horizon frequencies. Each QNM then has a driven and a free part, and the free part takes over only once the driving decays faster than the mode. The fundamental mode separates from the driving early. The overtones stay driven until the source is hidden behind the potential barrier, so overtone amplitudes fitted near the signal peak are in general not those of free oscillations. In GW250114, a ringdown model of the fundamental mode plus the first horizon mode, $\omega=2\Omega_{\rm H}-i\kappa$, is preferred over the fundamental mode plus its first overtone, with Bayes factors between 2 and 30, for start times from $2M_f$ before to $8M_f$ after coalescence. The horizon-mode fit returns a remnant that is heavier and spins faster than the inspiral predicts, as expected from nonlinear backreaction: the horizon that emits the mode has not yet settled to its final mass and spin. Zero-noise injections of numerical-relativity-calibrated waveforms reproduce both the preference and the shift, which are therefore features of general relativity.

papers.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation. (i) Accessibility and selective access. Multimodal concept information is readable in intermediate states and selectively accessible as tasks require. We extend "readout carriers" from one name token to a token set to better capture and express concept information and support counterfactual experiments. (ii) Concepts in downstream computation. Counterfactual experiments show that accessed concept information participates in downstream computation and reasoning. (iii) Development of cross-modal alignment and selective access. We develop two J-space metrics tracking the development of cross-modal concept alignment more clearly than hidden state cosine in controlled VLM training. The experiment also shows that reliable selective access develops later than concept accessibility. (iv) Shared functions across models. Across VLM families and sizes, we find shared patterns of concept accessibility, query-dependent selectivity and cross-task intervention effects despite differences in internal organisation. These findings offer an experimental basis to study GWT in multimodal artificial systems and how it can guide cross-modal alignment improvements.

papers.title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
papers.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear} when the {\em crossing of many-body energy levels} of bright and dark excitons occurs via phonon mediation. It also resembles the so-called field-like spin-transfer torque (STT) in spintronics, but STT is driven there with current pulses, so it explains the microscopic origin of the recently experimentally conjectured {\em excitonic STT}. Since dark excitons supply energy to magnons long after the fsLP is switched off, such a reservoir opens avenues for its engineering and applications in optospintronics and optomagnonics, neuromorphic computing, and quantum transduction.

papers.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
papers.abstract: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by the tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.

papers.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
papers.abstract: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.

papers.title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
papers.abstract: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. We present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. For $N$ layers, the representation contains $HW+N$ tokens before backbone-specific packing, compared with $NHW$ for full-grid-per-layer representations. ProtoDiffusion jointly denoises the prototype and a fixed set of candidate slots, conditioned on an image or text, with bounding boxes as optional layout guidance. The model leaves unneeded slots empty and determines the number of layers and, in absence of boxes, their layout, requiring neither as input. The same architecture supports both image-to-design and text-to-design. ProtoVAE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from its compact shared latent representation, reaching 40.43 dB PSNR on layer crops. On the LayerD evaluation split, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 scores of 0.040 with bounding boxes and 0.057 without, with box-guided alpha soft IoU (0.850) comparable to the strongest fine-tuned baseline (0.871). On merged images, text-to-design reaches 66.41 FID versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], achieves a 0.860 text-accuracy score, and runs $19.1\times$ faster than the same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.

papers.title: Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.

papers.title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
papers.abstract: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions. For judgments of whether German texts were written by a human or an AI, probes and word n-gram classifiers separated the classes well, but the answers did not and often ordered the texts inversely. Post-training lowered the sensitivity of the answers on average ($\Delta d' = -0.34$ across model families; -0.29 across three prompts). It also changed the use of a stated base rate: Base models shifted their log-odds by less than the stated change in prior odds, most post-trained models by more. In two models with stage-wise checkpoints, the change occurred during supervised fine-tuning, model stitching implicated the early layers, and from mid-depth on internal states at positions after the text, not those of the text, transferred the change between checkpoints. Our corpora cannot be shared, so we add a case reproducible from public data, the truth of negated statements. Here, post-training acted in the opposite direction: Probes decoded truth at or near ceiling in every model, the answers of several base models did not use it, and post-training repaired them; by mid-depth the repair resided at the positions after the statement; below it, the representation of the statement contributed, strongly in one of four models. In a training study, adding 2,000 correctly labeled authorship judgments of news texts to otherwise identical fine-tuning data improved the answers on our newspaper and textbook corpora and inverted them on the chats, where they followed a news-trained probe of the base model. Post-training thus changed how a judgment is read out of what a model represents, and a small training signal can set its direction.

papers.title: A Success Model at the End of Its Life Cycle: 30 Years of Regionalised Regional Rail in Germany
papers.abstract: On 1 January 1996, Germany transferred responsibility for regional passenger rail services from the federal government to the states. Three decades later, passenger-kilometres have doubled and competitive tendering has lowered operating costs substantially, making regionalisation the most successful element of the German rail reform. Its organisational model, however, has reached the end of its life cycle: tenders now attract on average only 1.3 bids, 26 contracting authorities and some 60 transport associations maintain overlapping structures, rolling-stock procurement has repeatedly shifted risk onto passengers, and since the Court of Justice of the European Union struck down the German track-access charge cap in 2026, funding no longer covers the ordered service volume. This article reviews the motives and results of regionalisation, identifies three structural design flaws, and argues for a second reform: consolidating authorities, standardising rolling stock, deciding between a repaired market model and integrated public operation, and indexing funding to real infrastructure cost development. The submission contains an English translation followed by the German original.

papers.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear. Here we formalize the concept of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations as one that accepts classical inputs and returns classical outputs, and provide implementations for algorithmic primitives in constructing such algorithms. We present a tailored end-to-end quantum algorithm for the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation (PDE) with variable coefficients widely used in simulating a biomolecular system. We explicitly implement all aspects of the algorithm, from preparing an initial state to generating a quantum solution and estimating properties of the system. In particular, we develop a new discrete representation for variable-coefficient PDEs on a grid that enables efficient implementation of the operator oracle, and build on a recent technique based on optimal wavelet preconditioning to generate a quantum solution with a cost independent of the condition number of the discretized operator. We show the algorithm can be implemented by quantum circuits of size polylogarithmic in both the number of grid points $N_g$ and the inverse of the desired accuracy $\varepsilon$, with an overall gate cost polylogarithmic in $N_g$ and quasilinear in $1/\varepsilon$. We also show the classical preprocessing to construct the circuits has polylogarithmic cost in $N_g$ and $1/\varepsilon$. Our work provides a concrete end-to-end quantum algorithm for a PDE of practical value, demonstrates an exponential improvement in scaling with $N_g$ over classical methods, and provides a foundation for assessing its potential quantum advantage in practice.

papers.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
papers.abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

papers.title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
papers.abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-\beta.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $\beta$ as $\beta_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $\beta_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

papers.title: Activity-driven motion and deformation of a circular membrane domain
papers.abstract: Lipid bilayer membranes are nanometer-thin fluid interfaces characterized by both in-plane fluidity and lateral compositional heterogeneity. Cholesterol-rich liquid domains ("lipid rafts") are thought to regulate the spatial organization of membrane proteins and numerous cellular processes. While the passive diffusion and equilibrium shape fluctuations of membrane domains are well understood, much less is known about how the activity of molecular machines, such as protein pumps and enzymes, influences their mobility and deformation. Here, we analyze the dynamics of a membrane domain driven by an embedded molecular machine within the framework of two-dimensional Stokes flow. The molecular machine is modeled as a point singularity of the two-dimensional Stokes equations, including both rotational and irrotational singularities corresponding to force and source multipoles. We show that, despite being force-free, both force and source dipoles generate active flows that propel the membrane domain. For a force dipole undergoing rotational diffusion, the domain motion is diffusive at long times but exhibits a transient superdiffusive regime at intermediate times.

papers.title: Classically Trained Quantum Generative Models with Shared Training and Fine Tuning for Quantum Matter
papers.abstract: Ground-state measurement statistics characterize quantum matter. Selected correlations can guide the classical training of a quantum sampler even when sampling the full distribution is difficult. We ask whether training across related ground-state distributions helps the sampler reproduce their correlations more accurately. We train a hypernetwork to map Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles, sharing information across the phase diagram before local fine-tuning with additional reference data for quantum deployment. For classical training, we derive an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator of Fourier coefficients for circuits built from general Pauli rotations, with a cost that depends on the circuit generators. We also introduce a CDF-KL loss for comparing selected marginals. We study the Haldane Hamiltonian and transverse-field Ising model, using an automated search to select reference calculations near phase transitions. On the twelve-site chain, the adaptively pretrained hypernetwork matches the independent fits' final mean total variation distance in fewer local updates and continues to a lower error. On a 1,024-site chain and a 4 by 256 lattice, the fine-tuned circuits have lower squared maximum mean discrepancy from the reference distributions than the independent circuits at the evaluated point in each geometry. These results motivate shared training for preparing quantum samplers across a phase diagram and local fine-tuning.

papers.title: Modeling the gravitational wave spectrum from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe: constant-in-time and coherent-decay models
papers.abstract: We study the production of gravitational wave (GW) backgrounds from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe, following the Constant-in-Time (CiT) model, presented and validated against simulations of decaying turbulence in arXiv:2201.05630. We extend the CiT model to account for the source decay using a coherent description for the unequal-time correlator (UETC) of the source. We present a generic framework that allows us to study different types of sources. As examples, we discuss the applicability of this framework to the production of GWs from decaying MHD turbulence, sound waves, and bubble collisions in first-order phase transitions. We show that the validity of the CiT and the coherent-decay models presented in this work relies on long decorrelation times of the source. However, as the decorrelation timescale of the UETC becomes short, a resonant term grows on top of the GW spectrum predicted by the CiT model, as found, for example, in earlier analytical studies of GW production from turbulence and sound waves. This model is compatible with previous numerical results and explains why sound waves in a radiation-dominated fluid are more efficient than subrelativistic MHD turbulence in producing GWs, which is no longer the case for relativistic turbulence. The CiT model predicts a generic spectrum that scales as $k^3$ in the IR regime, develops a linear $k$ at intermediate frequencies, and decays as $k^{1-b_\Pi}$ at frequencies above the inverse correlation length scale of the source, where $b_\Pi$ is uniquely determined by the type of source and the UV slope of its spectrum. Since the $k^3$ and $k$ scalings always appear for slowly-evolving sources and they are commonly found in studies of GW production, we motivate checking the potential applicability of the CiT to other sources of GWs.

papers.title: Stochastic counterpart of Nesterov's method for sampling and provable non-acceleration of samplers with heavy-ball structure
papers.abstract: Polyak's heavy-ball method and Nesterov's method are two momentum-based methods that have inspired many optimization techniques used in applied fields, including machine learning. Momentum also provides a connection with sampling, and interestingly, many kinetic Langevin samplers reduce to the heavy-ball recurrence when velocity is eliminated and noise is removed. This observation motivates a natural question: what is the corresponding sampler for Nesterov's method? We propose a sampler whose deterministic part is exactly Nesterov's recurrence, driven by temporally correlated Gaussian noise and requires one new gradient evaluation per step. Noise correlation provides $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ bias for smooth observables. We establish geometric ergodicity for possibly non-convex potentials. For strongly convex potentials with Lipschitz continuous gradients, we obtain contraction rates and show that, up to an additive constant, the energy decays at a rate of order $\kappa^{-1/2}$, where $\kappa$ is the condition number. For Gaussian targets, we show that relaxation has square-root dependence on $\kappa$. We further prove that any sampler based on heavy-ball dynamics with additive noise cannot achieve accelerated convergence uniformly over the class of strongly convex functions. Finally, we compare the proposed sampler with OBABO, BAOAB, HMC, MALA, BPS, and NUTS in numerical experiments and demonstrate the better performance of proposed sampler.

papers.title: Classical Oracle Separation of QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy and Quantum Cryptography Even When P = QCMA
papers.abstract: Remark: This work is in submission at STOC'27 and thus the full manuscript has been publicly posted on the conference website since November 3rd, 2026. Inspired by the Codeword-Hash Structure problem recently introduced by Cakan (arXiV, 2026) to separate $\mathsf{QMA}$ from $\mathsf{QCIP}$, we introduce a new problem called Codeword-Hash pairs in Noise ($\mathsf{CHN}$) and prove that, in the query complexity model, it is in $\mathsf{QMA}$ but hard for the $\mathsf{QCMA}$ hierarchy $\mathsf{QCMAH} = \bigcup_{d\geq1}\mathsf{QCMA}^{\mathsf{QCMA}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{QCMA}}}}$, the classical-witness quantum-verifier analogue of $\mathsf{PH}=\bigcup_{d\ge1}\mathsf{NP}^{\mathsf{NP}^{\cdots^{\mathsf{NP}}}}$. Using this problem, we show that there exists a classical oracle ${O}$ such that $\mathsf{P}^{{O}}=\mathsf{BQP}^{{O}}=\mathsf{QCMA}^{{O}} =\mathsf{QCMAH}^{{O}} \subset \mathsf{QMA}^{{O}} \text{ but } \mathsf{QMA}^{{O}}\not\subseteq\mathsf{QCMAH}^{{O}},$ thus showing that quantum state or quantum proof advantage could exist even if classical computers can efficiently solve any problem that can be quantumly verified with a classical proof. Further, using our problem, we show that various quantum cryptographic primitives can exist even when $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{QCMA}$ and thus neither quantum-computable one-way functions nor (verifiable) quantum computational advantage exist. In particular, relative to a classical oracle ${O}$ with $\mathsf{P}^{{O}}=\mathsf{BQP}^{{O}}=\mathsf{QCMA}^{{O}}=\mathsf{QCMAH}^{{O}}$, there exist pseudorandom states with classical keys and public-key encryption with copy-protected quantum decryption keys and classical public keys and ciphertexts, among other primitives, answering an open question of Kretschmer, Qian, and Tal (STOC 2025).

papers.title: Neighbourhood Walkability and Cardiometabolic Morbidity in Greater London: A Fine-Grained Spatial Analysis
papers.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases are leading causes of ill health, and neighbourhoods that support everyday walking may help reduce them. Studies often report lower disease prevalence in more walkable neighbourhoods. However, because walkability operates across multiple spatial scales, city-wide associations may conflate local neighbourhood form with broader metropolitan structure and co-varying environmental exposures. Here we show that while much of the walkability--morbidity association in Greater London operates through the city's macro-scale spatial structure, local alignment persists beyond it. Using an open five-component walkability index for 4,994 London census units and recorded prevalence of eight cardiometabolic conditions from primary-care registers, we found that higher walkability was inversely associated with all eight outcomes after adjusting for demographic composition and deprivation; one standard deviation higher walkability corresponded to 1.43 percentage points lower hypertension prevalence.
